docs.text: Architecture High-level components Frontend: React + Vite + TypeScript Backend API: FastAPI + MONAI + PyTorch Auth service: Django + Postgres Storage: local filesystem for uploads, outputs, and model bundles Chatbot: RAG pipeline backed by Chroma and Gemini (Google SDK) Segmentation data flow flowchart LR U[User] --> FE[Frontend] FE -->|Upload| BE[Backend API] BE -->|Store| UP[(Uploads)] FE -->|Start job| BE BE --> INF[Inference] INF --> OUT[(Outputs)] FE -->|Poll results| BE FE -->|Download outputs| BE Viewer data flow 2D slices: frontend requests PNG slices from /api/uploads/slice . 3D volume: frontend requests a NIfTI volume from /api/uploads/volume-file . 3D mesh: frontend requests a PLY mesh from /api/uploads/mesh . Chatbot data flow flowchart TD Q[User question] --> FE[Frontend chat UI] FE -->|POST /api/chat| BE[FastAPI chatbot route] BE --> RAG[RAG service singleton] RAG --> EMB[SentenceTransformer embed] RAG --> DB[Chroma vector store] DB --> RAG RAG --> LLM[Gemini model] LLM --> RAG RAG --> BE BE --> FE Chatbot-specific notes: - get_chatbot() lazily initializes the RAG pipeline on first request. - If the vector store is empty, a background indexing thread starts and the response notes that sources are unavailable. - Chroma persistence uses CHROMA_PATH when set, otherwise backend/chroma_db (if chroma.sqlite3 exists) or backend/chroma_storage . Auth boundary The backend enforces JWT auth for most endpoints. Exempt paths include: - /api/health - /api/chat , /api/chat/health , /api/chat/stats - /docs , /openapi.json Storage layout /data/uploads : raw uploads /data/outputs/<job_id> : segmentation outputs /data/tmp : temporary conversions /models/bundles : MONAI bundles and weights backend/chroma_db or backend/chroma_storage : Chroma persistence Key backend modules app/services/inference.py : segmentation pipeline app/services/models_registry.py : bundle discovery and metadata app/api/routes/uploads.py : uploads and viewer IO app/api/routes/segment.py : job creation and polling app/services/rag/chatbot.py : Gemini RAG logic Key frontend modules App.tsx : main UI, viewers, workspace ChatSidebar.tsx : slide-in assistant ChatPanel.tsx : full chat panel

docs.text: Auth and Roles Corpus Medica uses a dedicated Django auth service. Roles Developer: full control, can create admins and users. Admin: can create and manage users. User: standard access for clinicians. Key endpoints POST /api/token/ : login (username or email) GET /api/me/ : session check POST /api/email/verify/request/ POST /api/email/verify/confirm/ POST /api/password/forgot/ POST /api/password/reset/ Email verification Users must verify email before first login. Verification uses OTP over SMTP. Forgot password Requires a verified email. Uses OTP to confirm the reset. Admin setup Create the first developer account with Django: docker compose exec auth python manage.py createsuperuser Diagram flowchart TD A[Login] --> B{Email verified?} B -- No --> C[Block login + prompt verification] B -- Yes --> D[Issue tokens]

docs.text: Getting Started This guide gets the platform running locally for development or demo use. Prerequisites Docker Desktop (recommended for backend and auth service) Node.js 18+ (for frontend local dev) Python 3.11 (only if you run the backend outside Docker) Repo layout backend/ : FastAPI API + MONAI inference frontend/ : React UI auth_service/ : Django auth service models/ : MONAI bundles and weights Quick start (CPU) From the repo root: docker compose up --build Services: - Backend API: http://localhost:8000 - Auth service: http://localhost:9000 - Frontend (if running in Docker): http://localhost:5173 GPU build (optional) If you have a supported NVIDIA GPU: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.gpu.yml up --build Run frontend locally (recommended) From frontend/ : npm install npm run dev Set frontend/.env to point to the backend and auth service: VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000 VITE_AUTH_BASE_URL=http://localhost:9000 VITE_AUTH_REQUIRED=true Auth service settings Create .env from .env.example and add SMTP credentials: SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com SMTP_PORT=587 SMTP_USER=your@email SMTP_PASSWORD=your_app_password SMTP_FROM_EMAIL=your@email SMTP_USE_TLS=true SMTP_USE_SSL=false Model bundles If weights are not present in /models/bundles , download them once: docker compose exec backend python scripts/download_monai_bundles.py Common issues 401s from backend: ensure auth is enabled and you are logged in. Slow first chat response: initial indexing may take a few minutes. GPU errors: use the CPU build or reduce ROI size in the model config.

docs.text: Glossary Voxel: A 3D pixel representing a volume element. NIfTI: A neuroimaging file format for 3D medical images. DICOM: Standard format for medical imaging data and metadata. Modality: Imaging type such as MRI or CT. ROI: Region of interest used for inference or display. Colormap: Mapping of intensity values to colors. Iso-surface: A surface extracted from a volume at a constant value. Mesh: A surface representation built from vertices and faces. Affine: Matrix describing voxel-to-world alignment.

docs.text: Backend API Reference All routes are mounted under /api . Authentication Most endpoints require a Bearer token: Authorization: Bearer <access_token> The following are exempt: - /api/health - /api/chat , /api/chat/health , /api/chat/stats - /docs , /openapi.json Health GET /api/health Returns service status. Models GET /api/models Returns available models and metadata. Sample response: { "models": [ { "id": "brats_mri_segmentation", "name": "BraTS MRI Segmentation", "task": "brain_tumor_segmentation", "modality": "MRI", "available": true } ] } Uploads POST /api/uploads Upload a single file. Returns a saved path. POST /api/uploads/batch Upload multiple files (NIfTI or DICOM only). Returns a combined path. GET /api/uploads/preview Inspect the upload path and return file metadata. GET /api/uploads/volume-info Returns shape , channels , and zooms for a volume. GET /api/uploads/volume-file Returns a NIfTI volume for the selected channel. Query params: - path (required) - channel (default 0) GET /api/uploads/slice Returns a PNG slice. Query params: - path (required) - axis (axial, coronal, sagittal) - index - channel - colormap GET /api/uploads/mesh Returns a PLY mesh from a volume. Query params: - path (required) - channel - iso - step - label (optional) Segmentation POST /api/segment Starts a segmentation job. Request: { "saved_path": "/data/uploads/scan.nii.gz", "model_id": "brats_mri_segmentation" } GET /api/results/{job_id} Returns status, metrics, and outputs. GET /api/jobs Returns recent job history. Downloads GET /api/download Downloads an output file by path. Report analysis POST /api/reports/analyze Analyzes a report file or raw text payload. Chatbot (Gemini RAG) POST /api/chat Ask a RAG question. This endpoint always returns a JSON payload, even when the chatbot is not configured. Request: { "query": "How does BraTS preprocessing work?", "history": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi"} ], "top_k": 4 } Response: { "response": "Answer: ... Steps: ... Notes: ... Sources: ...", "sources": [ {"source": "backend/app/services/inference.py", "type": "python_code", "score": 0.84} ] } Notes: - top_k is validated between 1 and 8, but the RAG layer clamps to 4 ( MAX_TOP_K ). - Only the last 4 messages are used in the prompt ( MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGES ). - If GEMINI_API_KEY is missing, a configuration message is returned with empty sources . - If the RAG service cannot import, a fallback message is returned (also with empty sources ). GET /api/chat/health Returns config status and index state. Example response: { "chatbot_enabled": true, "api_key_configured": true, "rag_service": "available", "knowledge_base_indexed": true, "documents_count": 120 } Notes: - rag_service can be available , not_installed , or error: <message> . - knowledge_base_indexed and documents_count appear only when the RAG service is available. GET /api/chat/stats Returns collection stats: { "indexed": true, "documents_count": 120, "collection_name": "corpus_medica_docs", "status": "ready" }

docs.text: RAG Chatbot (Gemini) This module provides the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) assistant that answers questions about the Corpus Medica codebase, MONAI bundles, and workflows. The system is designed to be a developer and ops assistant, not a clinical decision tool. What it is (and is not) It is a repository-aware assistant with source citations when the index is ready. It is not a diagnostic engine and should not be used to interpret patient data. When the index is empty or still building, it falls back to general knowledge and tells the user that sources are unavailable. Primary entry points backend/app/api/routes/chatbot.py : /api/chat , /api/chat/health , /api/chat/stats endpoints. backend/app/services/rag/__init__.py : get_chatbot() singleton loader. backend/app/services/rag/chatbot.py : Gemini calls, Chroma store, retrieval logic. backend/app/services/rag/document_processor.py : file loading, filtering, chunk rules. Dependencies google-generativeai : Gemini SDK used via genai.GenerativeModel . chromadb : persistent vector store for embeddings. sentence-transformers : local embedding model for retrieval. Environment variables GEMINI_API_KEY (required): Gemini API key used by the SDK. CHROMA_PATH (optional): overrides the default Chroma persistence directory. If GEMINI_API_KEY is missing or a placeholder, /api/chat returns a setup message instead of calling Gemini. Gemini configuration and model selection Initialization tries a fallback list of model names in order until one works: - gemini-2.5-flash - models/gemini-2.5-flash - gemini-1.5-pro-latest - gemini-1.5-flash-latest - gemini-pro - models/gemini-1.5-pro-latest - models/gemini-1.5-flash-latest - models/gemini-pro The first model that initializes is used for all subsequent requests in that process. The model is created with the Google SDK (not a custom REST client). Generation configuration temperature = 0.2 for lower variance responses. max_output_tokens = 650 to keep answers compact for UI panels. Lazy initialization and lifecycle The RAG chatbot is initialized lazily: - The first call to get_chatbot() builds the singleton instance. - That first call loads the embedding model, connects to Chroma, and initializes Gemini. - This means the first chat request can be slower due to model load time. Vector store and persistence Chroma persistence is resolved in this order: 1) If CHROMA_PATH is set, use it. 2) Else, if backend/chroma_db/chroma.sqlite3 exists, use backend/chroma_db . 3) Else, fall back to backend/chroma_storage . Chroma collection details: - Collection name: corpus_medica_docs - Space: cosine ( metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"} ) Embeddings Embedding model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Dimension: auto-detected via get_sentence_embedding_dimension() (typically 384) Embeddings are generated locally with SentenceTransformer.encode() . Indexing: what gets embedded The indexing pipeline is implemented in RAGChatbot.index_knowledge_base() and uses DocumentProcessor . Prioritized sources 1) Any chroma_db directories found at: - backend/chroma_db - chroma_db 2) BRATS_README.md at project root 3) backend/scripts/download_monai_bundles.py 4) All files in models/bundles/** 5) Backend source code ( backend/** ) 6) Frontend source code ( frontend/src/** ) File type filtering DocumentProcessor.should_process_file() allows only text-like files. Key extensions include: - .py , .md , .txt , .json , .yaml , .yml - .ts , .tsx , .js , .jsx , .html , .css - .sh , .bat , .ps1 , .sql , .toml , .ini Excluded paths Files are skipped if they match common exclusions: - .git , node_modules , .venv , __pycache__ - dist , build , .next , coverage - chroma_storage , chroma.sqlite3 Metadata stored per document Each document stores metadata that is later returned as sources: - source (relative path) - type (ex: python_code , monai_bundle , documentation ) - filename , extension - chunk_index (only for chunked content) Chunking rules and limitations Default chunk_size = 1500 characters Default chunk_overlap = 200 Current behavior: large files return only the first chunk for speed. The full chunk_text() logic exists but is not used for large files yet. Indexing lifecycle and background thread On each chat request, the system checks if the collection has documents. If the collection is empty, it starts a background indexing thread. While indexing, responses indicate that sources are not yet available. This avoids blocking the first request, but the first few answers may not include citations until indexing completes. Query flow (request to response) 1) Frontend sends query , history , top_k to /api/chat . 2) Backend checks GEMINI_API_KEY and loads the singleton chatbot if needed. 3) If indexed, retrieve context via Chroma. If not, index in background. 4) Build a prompt that includes: - Context snippets - Recent chat history - The new user question 5) Send the prompt to Gemini and return the response. 6) Return response text plus sources list with scores. History and top_k limits API validates top_k between 1 and 8. The RAG layer clamps to MAX_TOP_K = 4 . The prompt includes only the last MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGES = 4 chat messages. The frontend sends up to 6 messages and uses top_k=4 . Context limits Context is truncated to keep prompts small: - MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS = 1400 per retrieved document. - Context snippets end at word boundaries when truncated. Prompt format The system prompt enforces a structured, plain-text response: - Answer: 3 to 6 sentences. - Steps: short actionable steps (if applicable). - Notes: risks, caveats, or assumptions. - Sources: file paths or "None (indexing in progress)". Markdown is discouraged in the prompt. The exception is the fallback message from /api/chat when the RAG service cannot import (that message includes markdown). Response schema POST /api/chat returns: - response : a plain-text answer from Gemini. - sources : list of { source, type, score } objects. Score is computed as 1.0 - distance where distance is the cosine distance returned by Chroma. Health and stats endpoints GET /api/chat/health returns: chatbot_enabled api_key_configured rag_service status knowledge_base_indexed and documents_count (if available) GET /api/chat/stats returns: indexed documents_count collection_name status Operational workflows Common scripts in backend/ : - init_chatbot.py : setup checks and optional test run. - test_chatbot.py : CLI test without frontend. - reindex_vector_db.py : force rebuild of embeddings. - test_gemini_models.py : probe available Gemini models. Failure modes and diagnosis Missing GEMINI_API_KEY : /api/chat returns a setup response. Model mismatch: Gemini errors surface in the response text and backend logs. Empty collection: answer returns with Sources: None (indexing in progress) . Chroma errors: /api/chat/health reports rag_service as error: ... . Performance notes The first chat request is slowest due to model initialization. Indexing time scales with repo size and bundle count. Retrieval and prompt assembly are lightweight once indexed. MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS and MAX_TOP_K are tuned to limit latency. Security and privacy The index contains local code and docs. Do not index PHI. The chatbot is informational only and should be behind auth controls in production. Future improvements Full-file chunking (multi-chunk indexing for large files) Streaming responses for long answers Swapable vector stores (Qdrant or pgvector) Caching for repeated queries Multiple collections for different documentation domains

docs.text: GEMINI_API_KEY (required): Gemini API key used by the SDK. CHROMA_PATH (optional): overrides the default Chroma persistence directory. If GEMINI_API_KEY is missing or a placeholder, /api/chat returns a setup message instead of calling Gemini.
docs.title: Environment variables

docs.text: Initialization tries a fallback list of model names in order until one works: - gemini-2.5-flash - models/gemini-2.5-flash - gemini-1.5-pro-latest - gemini-1.5-flash-latest - gemini-pro - models/gemini-1.5-pro-latest - models/gemini-1.5-flash-latest - models/gemini-pro The first model that initializes is used for all subsequent requests in that process. The model is created with the Google SDK (not a custom REST client).
docs.title: Gemini configuration and model selection

docs.text: temperature = 0.2 for lower variance responses. max_output_tokens = 650 to keep answers compact for UI panels.
docs.title: Generation configuration

docs.text: The RAG chatbot is initialized lazily: - The first call to get_chatbot() builds the singleton instance. - That first call loads the embedding model, connects to Chroma, and initializes Gemini. - This means the first chat request can be slower due to model load time.
docs.title: Lazy initialization and lifecycle

docs.text: Chroma persistence is resolved in this order: 1) If CHROMA_PATH is set, use it. 2) Else, if backend/chroma_db/chroma.sqlite3 exists, use backend/chroma_db . 3) Else, fall back to backend/chroma_storage . Chroma collection details: - Collection name: corpus_medica_docs - Space: cosine ( metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"} )
docs.title: Vector store and persistence

docs.text: Embedding model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Dimension: auto-detected via get_sentence_embedding_dimension() (typically 384) Embeddings are generated locally with SentenceTransformer.encode() .
docs.title: Embeddings

docs.text: The indexing pipeline is implemented in RAGChatbot.index_knowledge_base() and uses DocumentProcessor .
docs.title: Indexing: what gets embedded

docs.text: 1) Any chroma_db directories found at: - backend/chroma_db - chroma_db 2) BRATS_README.md at project root 3) backend/scripts/download_monai_bundles.py 4) All files in models/bundles/** 5) Backend source code ( backend/** ) 6) Frontend source code ( frontend/src/** )
docs.title: Prioritized sources

docs.text: DocumentProcessor.should_process_file() allows only text-like files. Key extensions include: - .py , .md , .txt , .json , .yaml , .yml - .ts , .tsx , .js , .jsx , .html , .css - .sh , .bat , .ps1 , .sql , .toml , .ini
docs.title: File type filtering

docs.text: Files are skipped if they match common exclusions: - .git , node_modules , .venv , __pycache__ - dist , build , .next , coverage - chroma_storage , chroma.sqlite3
docs.title: Excluded paths

docs.text: Each document stores metadata that is later returned as sources: - source (relative path) - type (ex: python_code , monai_bundle , documentation ) - filename , extension - chunk_index (only for chunked content)
docs.title: Metadata stored per document

docs.text: Default chunk_size = 1500 characters Default chunk_overlap = 200 Current behavior: large files return only the first chunk for speed. The full chunk_text() logic exists but is not used for large files yet.
docs.title: Chunking rules and limitations

docs.text: On each chat request, the system checks if the collection has documents. If the collection is empty, it starts a background indexing thread. While indexing, responses indicate that sources are not yet available. This avoids blocking the first request, but the first few answers may not include citations until indexing completes.
docs.title: Indexing lifecycle and background thread

docs.text: 1) Frontend sends query , history , top_k to /api/chat . 2) Backend checks GEMINI_API_KEY and loads the singleton chatbot if needed. 3) If indexed, retrieve context via Chroma. If not, index in background. 4) Build a prompt that includes: - Context snippets - Recent chat history - The new user question 5) Send the prompt to Gemini and return the response. 6) Return response text plus sources list with scores.
docs.title: Query flow (request to response)

docs.text: API validates top_k between 1 and 8. The RAG layer clamps to MAX_TOP_K = 4 . The prompt includes only the last MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGES = 4 chat messages. The frontend sends up to 6 messages and uses top_k=4 .
docs.title: History and top_k limits

docs.text: Context is truncated to keep prompts small: - MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS = 1400 per retrieved document. - Context snippets end at word boundaries when truncated.
docs.title: Context limits

docs.text: The system prompt enforces a structured, plain-text response: - Answer: 3 to 6 sentences. - Steps: short actionable steps (if applicable). - Notes: risks, caveats, or assumptions. - Sources: file paths or "None (indexing in progress)". Markdown is discouraged in the prompt. The exception is the fallback message from /api/chat when the RAG service cannot import (that message includes markdown).
docs.title: Prompt format

docs.text: POST /api/chat returns: - response : a plain-text answer from Gemini. - sources : list of { source, type, score } objects. Score is computed as 1.0 - distance where distance is the cosine distance returned by Chroma.
docs.title: Response schema

docs.text: GET /api/chat/health returns: chatbot_enabled api_key_configured rag_service status knowledge_base_indexed and documents_count (if available) GET /api/chat/stats returns: indexed documents_count collection_name status
docs.title: Health and stats endpoints

docs.text: Common scripts in backend/ : - init_chatbot.py : setup checks and optional test run. - test_chatbot.py : CLI test without frontend. - reindex_vector_db.py : force rebuild of embeddings. - test_gemini_models.py : probe available Gemini models.
docs.title: Operational workflows

docs.text: Missing GEMINI_API_KEY : /api/chat returns a setup response. Model mismatch: Gemini errors surface in the response text and backend logs. Empty collection: answer returns with Sources: None (indexing in progress) . Chroma errors: /api/chat/health reports rag_service as error: ... .
docs.title: Failure modes and diagnosis

docs.text: The first chat request is slowest due to model initialization. Indexing time scales with repo size and bundle count. Retrieval and prompt assembly are lightweight once indexed. MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS and MAX_TOP_K are tuned to limit latency.
docs.title: Performance notes

docs.text: The index contains local code and docs. Do not index PHI. The chatbot is informational only and should be behind auth controls in production.
docs.title: Security and privacy

docs.text: Full-file chunking (multi-chunk indexing for large files) Streaming responses for long answers Swapable vector stores (Qdrant or pgvector) Caching for repeated queries Multiple collections for different documentation domains

docs.text: Report Analysis The report analysis module extracts structured findings from clinical text and PDFs. Pipeline components report_text_extractor.py : loads PDFs and extracts raw text report_parser.py : normalizes and structures key fields risk_engine.py : maps findings to risk tiers groq_explainer.py : optional LLM-based summary (if enabled) Pipeline flow 1) Accept file or raw text. 2) Extract and clean text. 3) Parse values and sections. 4) Score and prioritize risks. 5) Optionally generate a narrative explanation. API endpoint POST /api/reports/analyze Typical response includes: - Normalized findings - Abnormal flags - Risk tiers - Optional explanation Environment settings GROQ_API_KEY enables Groq explanation output. Error handling The endpoint returns clear messages for: - Empty or invalid files - Missing dependencies (like pdfplumber) - Missing or invalid API keys

docs.text: Segmentation Pipeline Model registry The backend discovers models from MONAI bundles and optional registry data. Each bundle provides: - configs/metadata.json for task and modality - configs/inference.json for input channels and transforms - models/model.pt for weights A model is marked available only when weights exist on disk. Input handling Supported inputs: - NIfTI (.nii, .nii.gz) - DICOM directory or zip - Multi-modal zip of aligned NIfTI files Validation checks: - Correct channel count for the model - Matching shape and affine across modalities - Supported file types only Bundle runner flow 1) Prepare input path (convert DICOM if needed). 2) Validate channels and alignment. 3) If multiple NIfTI files are provided, stack into a multi-channel volume. 4) Call monai.bundle.scripts.run with runtime overrides: - bundle_root - output_dir - injected datalist - device selection - num_workers = 0 for stability in Docker TorchScript runner flow 1) Load volume and normalize intensity. 2) Run direct or sliding-window inference. 3) Write mask and report JSON. Job lifecycle Jobs are created by /api/segment and tracked in memory. Typical states: - queued - running - done - error Outputs Each job writes to /data/outputs/<job_id> and produces: - A mask volume ( *.nii.gz ) - A JSON report with metrics Metrics Default metric is a volume estimate based on voxel count: volume_cm3 = mask_voxels * voxel_volume_mm3 / 1000 Common failures Channel mismatch for BraTS models Misaligned modalities in a zip GPU OOM for large ROI sizes
docs.title: Segmentation

docs.text: Uploads and Volume IO This module powers 2D and 3D viewing and provides a clean interface to stored scans. Path resolution and safety All viewer endpoints call a resolver that ensures the requested path lives under: - /data/uploads - /data/outputs Requests outside those roots are rejected. Upload and preview /api/uploads stores a file and returns a saved path. /api/uploads/preview inspects the path and returns a structured preview. Preview responses include the kind of file and warnings if the contents are not supported. Volume metadata /api/uploads/volume-info returns: - shape : x, y, z - channels : number of channels - zooms : voxel spacing The frontend uses this to set slider limits and channel dropdowns. Volume files for 3D rendering /api/uploads/volume-file serves a NIfTI file for a given channel. Key behavior: - .nii.gz is uncompressed for the viewer if needed. - If the volume is 4D, a temporary single-channel NIfTI is created for the selected channel. - If the input is a zip, it is extracted to a temp directory first. - If the input is DICOM, it is converted to NIfTI using dicom2nifti . Slice rendering /api/uploads/slice returns a PNG image for: - axis: axial, coronal, sagittal - index: slice index - channel: channel index - colormap: grayscale, hot, cool, viridis, etc The backend: 1) Parses axis and clamps index. 2) Loads the slice data. 3) Normalizes intensity. 4) Applies the colormap. 5) Returns a PNG. Mesh generation /api/uploads/mesh runs an iso-surface extraction and returns a PLY mesh. Key parameters: - iso : threshold used in marching cubes - step : downsample step for speed - label : optional mask value to extract The mesh is generated from a single channel volume and returned as a binary PLY for the frontend to load. Caching and temp files Zip extraction and DICOM conversion use temporary directories under /data/tmp . These are cleaned after use.
docs.title: Volume IO

docs.text: Frontend Overview The frontend is a single-page React app with a primary App.tsx and supporting components. Structure App.tsx : main UI, viewer logic, workspace, auth App.css : global styles and animations components/ChatSidebar.tsx : chat drawer components/ChatPanel.tsx : full chat view Environment variables VITE_API_BASE_URL VITE_AUTH_BASE_URL VITE_AUTH_REQUIRED Main UI sections Model selection Upload and preview Segmentation run and results 2D/3D viewer Report analysis panel Chatbot sidebar Auth gating When auth is required, the app blocks access until: - Token is valid - Email is verified Chat UI behavior The sidebar chat opens as a slide-in drawer with a canned welcome message. The chat panel provides a full-page chat layout with a larger welcome state and richer styling. Both use the same /api/chat endpoint and send a short history window (last 6 messages). The frontend always requests top_k=4 and renders citations when returned. Sources are expandable per response and shown with score and file path. Suggested questions appear when the chat history is empty. Chat request details Payload includes query , history , and top_k . Each history entry includes { role, content } . Errors are rendered inline as assistant messages.

docs.text: Viewers (2D and 3D) 2D slices viewer The 2D viewer renders slices by calling backend endpoints. Data flow 1) Frontend fetches /api/uploads/volume-info to get shape and channels. 2) User selects axis and slice index. 3) Frontend requests /api/uploads/slice with axis, index, channel, and colormap. 4) Backend returns a PNG slice. 5) Frontend updates the view. UI behavior Axis tabs switch between axial, coronal, and sagittal. Sliders clamp to the volume shape for each axis. Colormap selection is sent to the backend to keep rendering consistent. Optional prefetch logic reduces lag while scrubbing. 3D volume viewer The 3D volume viewer uses a WebGL pipeline with vtk.js. Data flow 1) Frontend requests /api/uploads/volume-file for the current channel. 2) NIfTI is loaded into a VTK image data object. 3) A volume mapper and volume actor are created. 4) Transfer functions map intensity to color and opacity. 5) The renderer updates the viewport. UI controls Rotate, zoom, pan Opacity slider and colormap preset Clipping axis and slider for interior inspection Performance notes The viewer is lazily initialized on first use. Volume reloads are minimized by caching state. Downsampling and colormap adjustments happen without full reinit where possible. Sync behavior Viewer state is tied to the selected upload path and channel, ensuring the backend and UI stay aligned.

docs.text: Workspace The workspace is a dedicated area for deeper 2D and 3D exploration. Layout Fullscreen 3D viewport for mesh or volume Floating left and right shelves for tools Snap, drag, and resize behavior 3D mesh workspace Mesh is generated from volume data via /api/uploads/mesh . Mesh pipeline 1) Frontend requests a PLY mesh with iso and step parameters. 2) The PLY is parsed and converted to a renderable geometry. 3) Materials and lights are applied based on presets. 4) Optional overlay meshes are loaded for segmentation results. Current controls Mesh source: scan or segmentation mask Overlay mesh: adjustable opacity and iso Iso and step controls for mesh quality Clipping controls by axis Explode and isolate tools Material presets and wireframe toggle Orbit, pan, zoom controls Use cases Inspect organ shape and surface detail Compare segmentation output against scan mesh Reveal internal structures using clipping 2D workspace Tools: - Brush and erase - Rectangle ROI - Measurement helpers - Label palette and opacity Annotations The workspace stores annotation state in memory and can export results for later review.
